title: Mapping-space criterion for a horn-cocartesian edge
statement:
Use quasicategories, right-pinched mapping spaces, spaces and coherent composition as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and inner fibrations and horn-cocartesian edges as in [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $p:E\to B$ be an inner fibration between quasicategories in a fixed universe, and let $s:x\to y$ be an edge of $E$. The edge $s$ is $p$-cocartesian in the horn-lifting sense if and only if, for every vertex $z$ of $E$, precomposition with $s$ and with $p(s)$ gives a homotopy pullback square
$$\begin{array}{ccc}
\operatorname{Map}_E(y,z)&\longrightarrow&\operatorname{Map}_E(x,z)\\
\downarrow&&\downarrow\\
\operatorname{Map}_B(p(y),p(z))&\longrightarrow&\operatorname{Map}_B(p(x),p(z)).
\end{array}$$
A homotopy pullback square of spaces means that the canonical map from its upper left corner to the path-space homotopy fiber product of the other three corners is a weak homotopy equivalence. No existence of other cocartesian lifts is assumed.
